name: Amlodipine
summary: A vascular-selective calcium channel blocker used widely for hypertension and angina because it relaxes arterial smooth muscle smoothly and predictably.
good: Hypertension when a long-acting, once-daily arterial vasodilator is desirable.
bad: Patients who already have troublesome ankle edema or hypotension.
clinicalPearls: Edema is the signature side effect — it often reflects arteriolar dilation rather than fluid overload.
mechanism: Blocks L-type calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle, lowering peripheral resistance and blood pressure.
indications: Hypertension, chronic stable angina, and vasospastic angina.
interactionNotes: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors can raise exposure; combining with other rate-lowering drugs requires clinical sense.

warnings: Peripheral edema, flushing, headache, and occasional gingival overgrowth are the usual limiting effects.
